extracted.intended_audience: regulatory analysts, small business stakeholders, and public commenters on the proposed rule (e.g., SBA/agency analysts, industry representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the economic impact of a proposed rule on small entities by industry and firm-size categories using tabulated metrics (counts, receipts, discounted first-year and annualized costs) and comparing cost-per-firm percentages to a 3% significance threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business Size Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The size standard used to define 'small' for each industry (expressed as a range of employees or dollar receipts), e.g., "Small Business Size Standard: 500-1,500 employees" or "$9.0 million-$47.0 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine which firms count as small entities in each industry and therefore which firms are covered by the small-entity impact assessment. Exhibits list the applicable size standard for each industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of firms in each firm-size category (e.g., Enterprises with 0-4 employees: 10,808).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw counts per category are reported in the industry exhibits and form the basis for share and aggregate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of firms as percent of small firms in industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of the industry’s small firms represented by each firm-size category (e.g., 57.2%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify whether a category constitutes a substantial number of small entities (see 'substantial number' criterion). Examples in the exhibits show percentages (e.g., 24.1%, 18.0%, 20.0%, 22.3%, 23.4%) used to characterize substantiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total number of employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate employees for the firms in the category (column labeled 'Total number of employees').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides scale/context for the affected firms; reported in each exhibit per size/receipts category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual receipts ($ million)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total annual receipts (in $ million) for the firms in the category (column labeled 'Annual receipts ($ million)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to calculate average receipts per firm and to express cost impacts as a percent of receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average receipts per firm ($)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average annual receipts per firm in the category (column labeled 'Average receipts per firm ($)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denominator for percent-of-receipts calculations (e.g., average receipts of $61,501 for enterprises with receipts below $100,000 in construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-year cost per firm with 7% discounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated one-time (first-year) cost per firm, discounted using a 7% discount rate (column labeled 'First-year cost per firm with 7% discounting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a dollar amount (e.g., $3,420). Used to assess immediate burden on firms; paired with the receipts percent metric to judge significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-year cost per firm as percent of receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: First-year cost expressed as a percentage of average receipts for the firm category (column labeled 'First-year cost per firm as percent of receipts').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary comparator for determining whether the first-year cost is a 'significant economic impact' on firms; the document treats values of 3.0% or greater as significant (see significance threshold). Example: 5.6% for construction firms with receipts below $100,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annualized cost per firm with 7% discounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated annualized cost per firm (cost spread over time), calculated with a 7% discount rate (column labeled 'Annualized cost per firm with 7% discounting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a dollar amount (e.g., $3,238). Used to assess recurring/ongoing burden and compared to receipts percent for significance evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annualized cost per firm as percent of receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Annualized cost expressed as a percentage of average receipts for the firm category (column labeled 'Annualized cost per firm as percent of receipts').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine whether ongoing costs impose a significant economic impact; compared against the 3% threshold (e.g., annualized 5.3% for some small-receipt categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant economic impact threshold (3 percent or more)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule interprets a 'significant economic impact' on a small entity as costs equal to or greater than 3 percent of average receipts: 'not expected to have a significant economic impact (3 percent or more)' or conversely 'estimated to have a significant economic impact (3 percent or more)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any first-year or annualized cost-per-firm percentage >= 3.0% is treated as a significant impact for the purposes of the analysis; exhibits explicitly call out industry/category combinations meeting or not meeting this threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial number of small entities (qualitative/substantive consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether affected firms constitute a 'substantial number of small entities' in the industry, illustrated by statements such as 'those firms constitute a substantial number of small entities in the [industry] (24.1 percent)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exhibits pair the percent-of-small-firms column with the significance threshold to determine combined effect: high percentages (examples ~18–24%) are treated as 'substantial' in these findings. The page uses both the share-of-firms and percent-of-receipts metrics together to conclude whether the impact is significant and widespread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm grouping by employee ranges or receipts ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Firms are stratified into categories either by employee-size ranges (e.g., 0–4, 5–9, 10–19, 20–99, etc.) or by receipts ranges (e.g., receipts below $100,000; $100,000–$499,999; etc.), depending on industry conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping enables targeted impact estimates for the smallest firms versus larger small firms; conclusions frequently focus on the lowest-receipt categories (e.g., 'firms with receipts under $100,000').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a 7% discount rate in cost calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: All first-year and annualized cost estimates are presented 'with 7% discounting' (explicitly stated in column headers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the discounting methodology for present-value and annualized cost computations; analysts and reviewers should apply or understand the 7% discount rate when reproducing or evaluating the cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-level exhibit conclusion statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each industry exhibit is summarized with a plain-language conclusion about whether the first-year and annualized costs are expected to have a significant economic impact on small entities of any size or on specific firm-size categories (e.g., '...are not expected to have a significant economic impact (3 percent or more) on small entities of any size' or '...are estimated to have a significant economic impact (3 percent or more) on small entities with receipts under $100,000').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These narrative conclusions synthesize the tabulated metrics (counts, averages, percent-of-receipts) and identify the industry/category combinations warranting special attention in the regulatory flexibility analysis.
